newsitem.title: Syria: Syria denounces Washington over arms deal row.
newsitem.headline: Syria denounces Washington over arms deal row.

text.p: Syria on Wednesday slammed the United States for warning South Africa against selling arms to Damascus, cautioning Washington that it was harming its credibility in the Middle East.
"Once again the U.S. spokesman directs unjustified and harmful accusations at Syria which aim at nothing but to please Israel..," an official spokesman said in a statement.

"He is thus harming the credibility of the U.S. role as an honest broker which is required to make the peace process a success.. this process which Syria was and still is committed to in accordance with U.N. resolutions and the land for peace principle," he said.
He said the weapons which Syria intends to buy from South Africa were for defensive needs and hailed South African President Nelson Mandela's rejection of the U.S. pressure.
Washington on Monday warned it might be forced to cut aid to South Africa if Pretoria went ahead and sold Syria $641 million in tank-gun aiming gear.
But Mandela on Wednesday told reporters:"We will conclude agreements with any country whether they are popular in the West or not. And that is what we are likely to do in this case."
The United States is sponsoring peace talks between Syria and Israel which began in 1991 but which made no progress since then.
The Syrian spokesman expressed surprise that Washington was trying to prevent Syria from possessing weapons while Israel has a big modern arsenal.
"...the U.S. puts pressure on one country after another to deny Syria its natural right to possess the minimum level of methods for legitimate self defence," the spokesman said.

"It is regrettable that pressure is being practised against South Africa -- after it was liberated from apartheid and abandoned its nuclear weapons -- to prevent it from concluding commercial dealing with Syria and selling it some ordinary weapons," he said.

"The world still remembers how U.S. spokesmen used to be silent regarding the close military cooperation which existed between Israel and the previous racist regime of South Africa especially in nuclear armaments," he said.
In a reference to Washington's charges of Syria sponsoring terrorism, the Syrian spokesman said the U.S. should not try to apply its local rules and laws to other countries.
